name: Qwen3-Coder-Next (80B-A3B, non-thinking agentic coder)

official_org.value: Qwen (Alibaba Qwen team). The HF org 'Qwen' has 469 models, 116k followers and a team plan, but the HF API reports isVerified=false, so there is no verified badge. Ownership is backed by other evidence. The card links the blog https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3-coder-next and github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-Coder. That GitHub repo hosts the tech report, committed 2026-02-03. Unsloth's GGUF metadata records base_model organization = Qwen.

release_date.value: HF createdAt 2026-01-30T15:08:18Z (lastModified 2026-02-03). The public announcement was 2026-02-03: the tech report was committed to QwenLM/Qwen3-Coder that day, the card citation says 'Accessed: 2026-02-03', and Artificial Analysis gives releaseDate 2026-02-03. Both dates fall inside 2025-11-15..2026-11-15.

license.value: Apache-2.0. The card front matter reads 'license: apache-2.0' with license_link https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next/blob/main/LICENSE. This is a permissive license with no use-based restrictions; only the usual Apache notice and attribution terms apply.

params.value: 79.67B total by the HF API safetensors count (BF16 79,674,391,296). The card says '80B in total and 3B activated' and 79B non-embedding. Arithmetic on config.json: routed experts hold 48 layers x 512 x 3 x 2048 x 512 = 77.3B, about 97% of all weights. The BF16 safetensors total 159.36 GB (148.41 GiB).

architecture.value: Qwen3NextForCausalLM (model_type qwen3_next), a hybrid MoE with 48 layers, hidden size 2048 and full_attention_interval 4. The card describes the layout as 12 x (3 x (Gated DeltaNet -> MoE) -> 1 x (Gated Attention -> MoE)), so 12 layers use full attention with 16 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head_dim 256 and rotary dim 64 (partial_rotary_factor 0.25). The other 36 layers are Gated DeltaNet linear attention (32 V heads, 16 QK heads, head dim 128, conv kernel 4). Each MoE layer has 512 experts, 10 routed per token plus 1 shared, with expert intermediate size 512. There is no sliding window, rope_theta is 5e6 and rope_scaling is null.

context_length.value: 262,144 native (max_position_embeddings 262144; the card says 'Context Length: 262,144 natively'). Neither the card nor config.json documents a YaRN or extended-context setting (rope_scaling null). The card suggests 32,768 if you hit OOM.

modalities.value: Text in, text out. The checkpoint is text-only (CausalLM with no vision tower), and Ollama lists 'Text' input.

thinking.how_to_toggle: There is nothing to toggle. The card says: 'This model supports only non-thinking mode and does not generate <think></think> blocks in its output. Meanwhile, specifying enable_thinking=False is no longer required.' The chat template has no enable_thinking branch. vLLM needs no --reasoning-parser. llama.cpp needs no reasoning flag (output goes to content). The Ollama tag has no 'thinking' capability.

tool_calling.format:
Qwen3-Coder XML: <tool_call>
<function=NAME>
<parameter=ARG>
value
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>. Tool results go back as <tool_response> inside a user turn.
tool_calling.evidence: chat_template.jinja renders the tools list. When tools are passed it writes '# Tools ... <tools><function><name>..</name><description>..</description><parameters><parameter>..' plus an instruction block giving the XML call format, and it renders assistant tool_calls and tool messages. The card has an 'Agentic Coding' section with an OpenAI tools example and names Claude Code, Qwen Code, Cline and Kilo as supported scaffolds; its vLLM command uses --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder. The repo also ships qwen3coder_tool_parser_vllm.py and qwen3_coder_detector_sgl.py. In vLLM v0.33.0, tool_parsers/__init__.py maps qwen3_coder (and qwen3_xml) to Qwen3EngineToolParser. In llama.cpp b12418, common/chat.cpp:1420-1427 picks the specialized 'Qwen3-Coder' handler when the template contains <tool_call>, <function= and <parameter=, which this template does.

vllm.arch_supported: Yes. At tag v0.33.0, registry.py line 118 maps "Qwen3NextForCausalLM": ("qwen3_next", "Qwen3NextForCausalLM") and line 735 maps Qwen3NextMTP. docs/models/supported_models.md:468 lists Qwen3NextForCausalLM with LoRA and PP marked supported.
vllm.min_version: Card: vllm>=0.15.0 (sglang>=0.5.8). v0.33.0 is far above that.
vllm.best_checkpoint: None fits on the GPU. The smallest vLLM-loadable 4-bit build is Intel/Qwen3-Coder-Next-int4-AutoRound at 40.53 GiB (with open bug #59248). Next are RedHatAI/Qwen3-Coder-Next-NVFP4 at 44.30 GiB and cyankiwi AWQ at 44.93 GiB.
vllm.kv_math: Budget: 16303 MiB x 0.92 = 14999 MiB = 14.65 GiB. Minus a 1.2 GiB reserve leaves 13.45 GiB for weights plus KV. The smallest checkpoint is 40.53 GiB (int4 AutoRound) and NVFP4 is 44.30 GiB, so the KV pool is about -27 GiB and the model does not fit. KV per token if it did: 2 x 12 full-attention layers x 2 KV heads x 256 head_dim x 2 B = 24,576 B (24 KiB) at BF16, or 12,288 B at FP8. Gated DeltaNet holds a fixed per-sequence state: 36 layers x 32 x 128 x 128 recurrent state, about 72 MiB at fp32. At 262,144 tokens the KV is 6.0 GiB at BF16 or 3.0 GiB at FP8. vLLM v0.33.0 has UVA weight offload (--cpu-offload-gb N --cpu-offload-params experts, vllm/config/offload.py). It would need about 31+ GiB of pinned host RAM, and every forward pass would stream expert weights over PCIe. No source shows this working for this model on sm_120 (speculative).
vllm.quant_on_sm120: Not exercised because the model does not fit. Per the lead's discovery, NVFP4 on sm_120 uses FlashInfer CUTLASS / b12x kernels. Open issue #66423 reports a segfault at engine init with any --reasoning-parser on SM120 + NVFP4 W4A4 (flashinfer_cutlass MoE). This model needs no reasoning parser.
vllm.tool_call_parser: qwen3_coder (Qwen3EngineToolParser in v0.33.0 vllm/tool_parsers/__init__.py:206; qwen3_xml is the same class)
vllm.serve_command: Card command, written for 2+ GPUs and not usable on this machine: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder
vllm.known_issues: Open vLLM issues: #34322 (2026-02-11, Qwen3-Coder-Next + qwen3_coder parser IndexError: list index out of range); #57699 (qwen3_coder drops the last parameter when </parameter> is missing); #65774 (a repeated parameter breaks streamed tool-call arguments); #57541 (<tool_call> inside fenced code is parsed as a call); #59248 (AutoRound routed MoE gate ignores quantization); #62320 (b12x attention backend cannot serve hybrid attention/mamba models in v0.32.0).

llamacpp.arch_supported: Yes. At b12418, src/llama-arch.cpp:42 has LLM_ARCH_QWEN3NEXT "qwen3next", and the HF API reports gguf.architecture qwen3next for the Qwen and unsloth repos. Note that GitHub releases/latest now returns a non-prerelease tag v1.0.0 (2026-11-13), while the b124xx builds are flagged prerelease.
llamacpp.quant: UD-IQ4_XS (38.43 GB / 35.79 GiB). The quality step up is UD-Q4_K_XL (46.20 GiB) or the official Q4_K_M (45.19 GiB); both are feasible but tight. The step down is UD-Q3_K_XL (33.79 GiB).
llamacpp.offload_plan: Tensor split comes from parsing the GGUF headers with HTTP range reads; per-layer figures are the expert total divided by 48. UD-IQ4_XS: experts 33.38 GiB (0.695 GiB/layer), non-expert 2.41 GiB (embd/out 0.55 + attention/DeltaNet/norms 1.71 + shared experts 0.15). GPU budget is about 16303 MiB - 112 idle - 1 GiB --fit margin, about 15.0 GiB. On GPU: non-expert 2.41 + KV at 131072 ctx F16 3.0 GiB (24 KiB/token; q8_0 1.59 GiB) + DeltaNet state about 0.08 + compute buffers about 1.5 = about 7.0 GiB. That leaves about 8 GiB, enough for 11 expert layers (7.65 GiB), so --n-cpu-moe 37 and about 14.3 GiB on the GPU. In RAM: 37 x 0.695 = 25.7 GiB of the about 40 GiB free (comfortable). At 262144 ctx with -ctk/-ctv q8_0 (3.19 GiB KV) the same split holds. Official Q4_K_M (45.19 GiB): non-expert 1.60, 0.908 GiB/layer, about 9 layers on GPU, so --n-cpu-moe 39 puts 35.4 GiB of experts in RAM, leaving only about 4.6 GiB headroom against 40 GiB free. That is feasible but tight: with mmap, desktop memory growth evicts expert pages and they are re-read from NVMe (stalls). Plain --cpu-moe on Q4_K_M puts all 43.6 GiB of experts in RAM, which exceeds the free RAM and is not recommended. UD-Q4_K_XL: about 8 layers on GPU, 36.4 GiB in RAM, also tight. --fit (on by default at b12418, 1 GiB target margin) can choose the split automatically.
llamacpp.server_command: docker run --rm --gpus all -p 8080:8080 -v $HOME/models:/models ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda13 -m /models/Qwen3-Coder-Next-UD-IQ4_XS.gguf --alias qwen3-coder-next --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 -c 131072 -ngl all --n-cpu-moe 37 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -np 1 -b 2048 -ub 2048 --jinja --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 40   (needs the NVIDIA Container Toolkit first; for 256K use -c 262144 and keep --n-cpu-moe 37)
llamacpp.tool_calling_note: --jinja is on by default (common.h:675). The template matches llama.cpp's specialized Qwen3-Coder XML handler (common/chat.cpp:1420-1427, b12418), so OpenAI tool_calls come back parsed. unsloth's embedded template drops '| safe' from the official one. Caveat: on hybrid Gated DeltaNet models the slot prefix cache depends on context checkpoints (--ctx-checkpoints, --cache-ram). Open issue #30357 shows non-canonical whitespace around <tool_call> forcing a full re-prefill on Qwen3.5+ hybrids; it was not shown for this template.

ollama.context: 256K context window listed for each tag. Ollama's default runtime context on GPUs under 24 GiB is 4k per the lead, so set OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH or num_ctx.
ollama.capabilities: tools only. There is no thinking badge and no vision; input is Text. The library page lists 'ollama launch opencode --model qwen3-coder-next'. On this machine 52 GB (about 48.4 GiB) is above the about 15 GiB VRAM + about 40 GiB free RAM comfort zone with whole-layer offload, so it is not recommended. Pulling an unsloth IQ4_XS via hf.co/... in Ollama is untested.

speed_notes: Inferred bandwidth arithmetic for UD-IQ4_XS with --n-cpu-moe 37 (no measured RTX 50-series reports were found). Per decoded token, each MoE layer reads 10/512 of its experts: 0.695 GiB x 10/512 = about 13.9 MiB per layer. The 37 RAM-resident layers read about 0.50 GiB (0.54 GB), which takes about 5.4-6.7 ms at 80-100 GB/s DDR5. The GPU reads the non-expert weights (about 2.4 GiB, of which about 2.1 GiB is really read because the embedding table is a lookup) plus 11 expert layers, about 2.6 GB, in about 3 ms at 896 GB/s. That puts the decode ceiling around 100-110 tok/s. Real CPU MoE efficiency is typically well below peak, so expect roughly 30-50 tok/s (speculative). For prompt processing with large ubatches, llama.cpp uploads the CPU-resident expert weights (25.7 GiB) to the GPU once per ubatch. At an effective 25-50 GB/s over PCIe 5.0 x16 (unverified for this laptop) that is about 0.5-1.1 s per 2048-token ubatch, roughly 2-4k tok/s prefill (inferred). --moe-cache-mib can cache hot experts in VRAM. Artificial Analysis gives a 70 tok/s output speed for hosted API providers only, which is not a local figure. Only 12 of the 48 layers carry a KV cache, so long contexts cost little bandwidth.

opencode_fit.recommended_runtime: llama.cpp server (ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda13) with --n-cpu-moe expert offload. vLLM does not fit. The Ollama q4_K_M at 52 GB is too large for comfort.
opencode_fit.recommended_checkpoint: unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF UD-IQ4_XS (35.79 GiB). Use the official Qwen Q4_K_M (45.19 GiB) only if about 36 GiB of RAM can be kept free.
opencode_fit.recommended_context: 131072 with q8_0 KV (262144 also fits at the same split with q8_0 KV, about 3.2 GiB)
opencode_fit.caveats: This is the strongest vendor-reported agentic coder in the candidate set (SWE-bench Verified 70.6-71.3, self-reported), and it is non-thinking with native Qwen3-Coder XML tool calls. It runs only with most experts in system RAM: 25.7 GiB at IQ4_XS, 35-36 GiB at Q4. Speed is therefore bounded by DDR5, and the RAM headroom shrinks as the desktop grows. Do not run it under the 32 GB heavy.slice cap with a Q4 file; Docker containers sit in their own cgroup. The NVIDIA Container Toolkit must be installed for --gpus. OpenCode v2.3.0 vLLM/llama.cpp discovery starts models with tools disabled, so tools must be enabled in the provider config (issue #60202). Hybrid DeltaNet prefix caching in llama.cpp depends on context checkpoints, and template whitespace mismatches can force a full re-prefill (#30357). Known qwen3_coder parser edge cases are open in vLLM (#34322, #57699, #65774). Sampling per the card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 40.

gaps: No measured tokens/s for Qwen3-Coder-Next on any RTX 50-series GPU with expert offload; speed figures are bandwidth arithmetic only.
The HF org 'Qwen' has isVerified=false in the HF API, so there is no verified badge; ownership is inferred from the card and GitHub links. The qwen.ai blog page is JS-rendered and was not read raw.
Compute buffer size (1.0-1.5 GiB) and the free RAM at serve time are estimates; the --n-cpu-moe value must be tuned on the machine (or let --fit decide).
Whether vLLM v0.33.0 UVA offload (--cpu-offload-gb with --cpu-offload-params experts) can serve this model on sm_120 with about 31 GiB pinned RAM was not established.
Ollama: whether its engine handles qwen3next from an external hf.co unsloth GGUF, and its MoE offload behaviour, were not verified.

The Artificial Analysis values were extracted from page JSON near the 'qwen3-coder-next' slug; the AA Intelligence Index is N/A for this model. No official SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench or BFCL leaderboard row for this model was checked.
Card benchmark images (benchmarks.png, swebench_pro.png) were not read; the numbers come from the tech report tables instead.
Quality loss of UD-IQ4_XS vs Q4_K_M for agentic tool calling is not measured by any primary source.
